title: Uber Tempe developmental ADS crash
system_purpose: Developmental ADS test vehicle operation on public roads
decision_impact: Vehicle control while a safety operator occupied the driver's seat
affected_groups: Pedestrian; safety operator; other road users
verified_facts: NTSB reported that an ADS-controlled test vehicle struck and fatally injured a pedestrian in Tempe. It found the operator's visual distraction was the probable cause and identified inadequate safety-risk assessment and ineffective operator oversight as contributing factors.
reported_harm: A pedestrian died. The investigation documents a real safety-management and operator-monitoring failure; it does not establish that a different console or pilot will cause the same event.
quantitative_evidence: The report records a 49-year-old pedestrian death; the ADS had operated about 19 minutes in autonomous mode and first detected the pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact.
limitations: A single US crash cannot quantify risk for a different system, route, sensor suite, operating policy, or Vietnam pilot. The report cannot validate SafeRoute's proposed thresholds.

title: NHTSA Tesla Autopilot recall-query and take-over-readiness evidence
system_purpose: Partial driving automation with driver controls and engagement features
decision_impact: Driver engagement, mode comprehension, and vehicle-control supervision during automated operation
affected_groups: Drivers; vehicle occupants; pedestrians; other road users
verified_facts: NHTSA's recall-query opening document says its earlier investigation identified at least 13 fatal crashes and many serious-injury crashes in which foreseeable driver misuse appeared to play a role, and it questioned the remedy. Separately, a 30-participant public-road study observed that forward-road attention did not return to the manual-driving baseline until after 15 seconds following a take-over request.
reported_harm: NHTSA describes fatal and serious-injury risk associated with apparent foreseeable misuse; the study makes delayed readiness a foreseeable human-factors hazard, not a confirmed cause of any NHTSA crash.
quantitative_evidence: NHTSA stated that at least 13 crashes involved one or more fatalities in its earlier investigation; the peer-reviewed study involved 30 participants and reported the 15-second attention result.
limitations: Tesla Autopilot is an SAE Level 2 comparator, the recall query was open, and the 30-participant Wizard-of-Oz study supplies no universal threshold. Neither source evaluates SafeRoute or developmental ADS testing.

title: California suspension of Cruise permits
system_purpose: Driverless deployment and driverless testing of autonomous vehicles
decision_impact: Permission to operate autonomous vehicles on public roads
verified_facts: California DMV immediately suspended Cruise's deployment and driverless-testing permits, effective immediately, and cited public-safety and safety-information grounds. The same statement said the action did not affect Cruise's testing permit with a safety driver.
reported_harm: The regulator action shows that safety-information and restart-governance failures can stop driverless operations. The statement alone does not establish a technical root cause or confirm physical harm from every cited event.
quantitative_evidence: The suspension took effect immediately on 2023-10-24; the DMV distinguished it from testing with a safety driver.
limitations: This is a driverless-operation comparator, not evidence that supervised pilots are unsafe. The public statement and enforcement record do not substitute for a complete causal analysis or a Vietnam approval decision.
